history.title: US Army assesses Trust Automation’s integrated drone defence system
history.originalTitle: US Army assesses Trust Automation’s integrated drone defence system

evidenceRecords.text: Trust Automation has completed a US Army operational assessment of its Small-Unmanned Air Defense System (SUADS) during a National Training Center rotation at Fort Irwin, California.

Conducted with the 703rd Brigade Support Battalion, 2nd Armored Brigade Combat Team, 3rd Infantry Division, the assessment evaluated SUADS in a large-scale combat operations training environment under ongoing uncrewed aerial system (UAS) threats.

During the rotation, Trust Automation’s SUADS detected and engaged UAS between approximately two and six kilometres away, with potential coverage extending to approximately seven kilometres under favourable conditions, the company said in a 12 October press release.
Trust Automation’s integrated system combined radar, electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) sensors, NINJA and DroneBuster technologies.
SUADS brings multiple sensors and effectors into a single integrated system while enabling individual technologies to be added or upgraded as capabilities and threats evolve.
Trust Automation is also developing a mobile SUADS variant to support tactical units where forces move frequently.
For more information Trust Automation The September issue of the 2026 Unmanned Airspace Global Counter-UAS Systems Directory is now available.
The post US Army assesses Trust Automation’s integrated drone defence system first appeared on Unmanned airspace .
Interview participants were not aware of any enemy UAS that penetrated the defended area as a threat within the identified operational ranges without first being detected by the system.

MAJ Patrick Smith, Battalion Executive Officer said the system consistently provided layered surveillance, early warning, positive target identification and electronic defeat of hostile UAS before enemy systems could successfully conduct reconnaissance, target acquisition or attack missions.

history.title: Kongsberg to build new plant in Poland for counter-drone systems
history.originalTitle: Kongsberg to build new plant in Poland for counter-drone systems

evidenceRecords.text: WARSAW, Poland — Norway’s Kongsberg has decided to build a new production facility for counter-drone systems in northern Poland, with plans to invest more than 200 million zloty ($51 million) in the plant.
The investment is connected to the company’s cooperation with Polish state-run defense group PGZ to deliver the San anti-drone system to the Polish military.
“We have been present in Poland for many years.

We think it’s important that we establish local sites in Poland,” Eirik Lie, the president and CEO of Kongsberg, told Defense News at the Warsaw Security Forum here on Oct. 12. “We are on good track for deliveries on the San program.
But also, we expect export contracts, so this enables us to be prepared for these exports from Poland.”

Under the San deal, valued at around PLN 15 billion ($3.8 billion), Kongsberg and PGZ are to supply 18 anti-drone batteries, 52 firing platoons, 18 command platoons, and 703 vehicles to the Polish military, according to data from Poland’s Ministry of National Defence.
The contract will be largely financed by loans that Poland has secured from the European Union’s Security Action For Europe (SAFE) scheme.
In a statement, the Norwegian group said it plans to sign a construction contract by the end of 2026 and begin work immediately afterward.
Serial production of counter-drone systems could begin in the first half of 2028.
The investment is expected to create more than 100 jobs in Poland once the plant reaches full capacity.

history.title: US Army targets 2028 for first high-energy laser counter-drone weapons
history.originalTitle: US Army targets 2028 for first high-energy laser counter-drone weapons

evidenceRecords.text: The first directed energy weapon selected by the U.S. Army for the Enduring-High Energy Laser (E-HEL) program could be out of testing and ready for counter-drone operations by early 2028, Army officials told Military Times at the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual meeting in Washington.

However, what we’ve seen is, with the environment as it is, everything that we produce as a capable counter-UAS system tends to get deployed somewhere,” said Kirk Williams, chief engineer at the U.S. Army Directed Energy Project Office.
In September, the Army awarded AeroVironment a $464.8 million contract for LOCUST X3, its modular, palletized high-energy laser system.
Earlier generations of the LOCUST system are actively fielded in operational environments, including at the U.S. southern border, according to AeroVironment.
The first LOCUST X3 is slated for delivery by Q4 of FY 2027 and will be mounted on the Joint Light Tactical Vehicle.
That would be a great win for the Army.” It is unclear where the first high-energy counter-drone weapons under H-ELS will be deployed.

The counter-drone E-HEL contract is for more than 26 laser weapons units total, according to AeroVironment vice president of Directed Energy, John Garrity, who indicated the initial system is on target for 2027 delivery.
“We would love to be able to keep the first unit off the line for our testing and training.
The goal is to push it through testing, validation, verification and “give it to soldiers as soon as possible,” said Brig.
Gen. Guy Yelverton, capability program executive for Defensive Fires. “My far-down point would be spring [2028], and if I could get in the December-January timeframe, that would be awesome.
That would be a great win for the Army.”
It is unclear where the first high-energy counter-drone weapons under H-ELS will be deployed.
Yelverton suggested the 7th Infantry Division could be a potential partner.

Deputy commanding officer of Support for the 7th Infantry Division, Col. Charles Kean, described directed-energy weapons as a component of defense against high-echelon air threats, including individual UAS or formations, but said they were not a “single bullet” solution.
The Royal Navy Type 45 Destroyers appear to have received a new C-UAS system for self protection against drones.
Images released recently by the UK MoD show HMS Dauntless (D33) sporting two mystery containers that are likely acting as interceptor drone launchers.
The Ukrainian Navy ships were closing out Exercise Lion Protector, demonstrating their ability to safely manoeuvre as a small task group in company with a major warship, played by Dauntless.

The apparent lack of new, organic sensors indicate that the interceptors must be receiving targeting data from the Type 45’s existing suite, i.e. the Sampson multi-function radar, the S1850M long-range radar on the aft mast and/or the electro optic systems.
Adapting to new threats The presence of this new system on a Type 45 destroyer shows how navies are adapting to the new challenges posed by affordable drones.
This suggests HMS Dauntless could be the first Type 45 ship to trial the capability ahead of her High North deployment.

Drone attack and swarming tactics—extensively practiced by the Royal Navy and French Navy in dedicated exercises like Sharpshooter and WildFire and based on their experience from Red Sea deployments—highlighted a critical limitation in European navies’ VLS magazine depth (48 cells for Type 45 and Horizon destroyers, 32 cells for French Air Defence FREMMs).
To address this issue, the Royal Navy started transitioning toward DragonFire lasers and C-UAS helicopter (Martlet / LMM aboard Wildcat) .

The new C-UAS system spotted on Dauntless shows that the Royal Navy continues to transform the Type 45 from a conventional air-defence vessel into a highly resilient platform capable of surviving drone saturation.

events.title: Powerus exhibits AI-enabled Guardian 3 C-UAS interceptor at AUSA 2026
events.originalTitle: Powerus exhibits AI-enabled Guardian 3 C-UAS interceptor at AUSA 2026
events.excerpt: Powerus Corporation has launched the company’s Guardian-3 counter drone interceptor this week at the Association of the United States Army’s 2026 Annual Meeting and Exposition, held October 12 to 14 in Washington, D.C. Guardian-3 features a new design built for fully autonomous operation, said the company in a press release. The Guardian 3 is understood to use artificial intelligence to navigate towards a threat once the threat has been identified then navigate to the target and strike using its on-board AI systems.

history.title: Energy Department Announces New Genesis Mission Awards to Accelerate Scientific Capability
history.originalTitle: Energy Department Announces New Genesis Mission Awards to Accelerate Scientific Capability

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief The Department of Energy announced $159 million for 12 new Phase II Genesis Mission projects using AI and advanced computing to accelerate scientific research.
The projects include Harvard -led quantum computing error correction, Oak Ridge-led quantum magnet design, and efforts in fusion energy, biotechnology, geothermal energy and particle physics.

PRESS RELEASE — The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced 12 Phase II project awards for President Trump’s historic Genesis Mission, totaling $159 million, that will expand efforts to harness artificial intelligence (AI), advanced computing, and the nation’s world-class scientific capabilities to accelerate the pace of discovery.

By connecting America’s leading scientists with advanced AI, supercomputing, scientific data and DOE’s unique research infrastructure, the Genesis Mission is creating new capabilities to accelerate scientific discovery and expand the frontiers of U.S. science and technology.
The Department of Energy announced $159 million for 12 new Phase II Genesis Mission projects using AI and advanced computing to accelerate scientific research.
The projects include Harvard-led quantum computing error correction, Oak Ridge-led quantum magnet design, and efforts in fusion energy, biotechnology, geothermal energy and particle physics.
The awards build on the Genesis Mission’s growing portfolio of projects, first announced in July, to address critical national science and technology challenges.

history.title: Guest Post: Quantum Computing’s Transistor Moment
history.originalTitle: Guest Post: Quantum Computing’s Transistor Moment

evidenceRecords.text: In 2023, fabrication of NV centers was demonstrated at production scale under Germany’s national quantum computing initiative – the “transistor” manufactured repeatably rather than hand-assembled one defect at a time.

That figure deserves attention because almost no competing spin-defect platform has published a fabrication yield at all, and yield is the industrial question – how reliably usable qubits can be placed where they are wanted, at scale.
The first is a transistor moment.
In 2020, researchers in Leipzig, Germany, demonstrated the first working one-qubit diamond-based quantum computer – proof that the device physics worked outside a research setting.
Diamond – The Silicon of Quantum Computing?
Whether NV-center diamond is quantum computing’s silicon – the material system that wins the platform war – is an open question.
Silicon-vacancy and tin-vacancy centers in diamond have so far worked only at cryogenic temperatures, and other spin centers could eventually prove better.

history.title: IonQ Agrees to Buy Elisity in Cybersecurity Deal Worth Up to $1.3 Billion
history.originalTitle: IonQ Agrees to Buy Elisity in Cybersecurity Deal Worth Up to $1.3 Billion

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief IonQ has agreed to acquire cybersecurity company Elisity in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion, according to The Wall Street Journal.
IonQ CEO Niccolo de Masi said the acquisition aims to help customers address growing cybersecurity risks associated with AI and quantum computing.

IonQ has agreed to buy cybersecurity company Elisity in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion, expanding its security business as advances in quantum computing and artificial intelligence raise concerns about cyberattacks.
The transaction includes up to $150 million in additional payments tied to Elisity’s future performance, executives told The Wall Street Journal .
IonQ Chairman and CEO Niccolo de Masi told the newspaper that the acquisition reflects his expectation that companies will need stronger defenses as both technologies become more powerful.
“With Elisity and its team as part of IonQ , we will be well positioned to help customers protect critical infrastructure and enterprise networks throughout the transition to the quantum era.
IonQ is offering its customers a vertically integrated full-stack quantum platform across quantum computing, networking, sensing and cybersecurity.

Just as adding SkyWater Technology expanded IonQ’s capabilities in chip design, fabrication and packaging, Elisity will bring proven enterprise policy enforcement scale and deployment experience to our quantum security strategy and will give IonQ a strong growth platform to serve customers and create value for our shareholders,” Niccolo de Masi, Chairman and CEO of IonQ, said in a statement .
The Elisity agreement follows IonQ ’s $1.8 billion deal earlier this year to acquire chipmaker SkyWater Technology, likely its largest acquisition to date.

Insider Brief Manipal Academy of Higher Education launched Manipal House of Quantum, Quantum-Hub@MAHE, at MIT Bengaluru to support quantum engineering, hardware experimentation and indigenous technology development in India.
PRESS RELEASE — Manipal Institute of Technology, Bengaluru (MIT Bengaluru) on Tuesday launched Manipal House of Quantum, Quantum-Hub@MAHE.
Venkatesh, VSM (Retd.), 7th Vice Chancellor, MAHE and Advisor to MEMG; Prof. (Dr.) Madhu Veeraraghavan, Pro Vice Chancellor, MAHE Bengaluru; Dr. Karunakar A.

Kotegar, Pro Vice Chancellor, Technology & Science, MAHE; Dr. Raghavendra Prabhu, Additional Registrar, MAHE Bengaluru; Prof. Iven Jose, Director, MIT Bengaluru; and Mr. Vishal Chatrath, Co-Founder & CEO, QuantrolOX .

Located at the MAHE Bengaluru campus, the quantum facility at MIT Bengaluru provides students, researchers and industry collaborators with hands-on access to advanced quantum computing infrastructure, including quantum hardware, cryogenic systems and quantum control technologies.

Through an integrated academic framework, the facility will support experimentation, application development, deep-tech start-up incubation, component innovation, testing and translational research, positioning MIT Bengaluru as an emerging centre for quantum engineering and indigenous hardware development.
The facility commences operations with a 25-qubit open-architecture dilution refrigeration system designed for advanced training and experimentation.
Rao, Vice Chancellor, MAHE, said, “The MAHE House of Quantum at MIT Bengaluru reflects MAHE’s commitment to building advanced scientific capabilities and nurturing talent in emerging technologies.

By creating access to modern quantum infrastructure, we aim to contribute meaningfully to India’s growing quantum ecosystem.” Prof. (Dr.) Madhu Veeraraghavan, Pro Vice Chancellor, MAHE Bengaluru, said, “The Hub brings together education, research and innovation on a common platform.

It will create opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and help translate academic research into real-world technological impact.” Prof. Iven Jose, Director, MIT Bengaluru, said, “The quantum facility at MIT Bengaluru will provide students and researchers with valuable exposure to real quantum systems and engineering environments.

It marks an important step towards developing the next generation of quantum scientists, engineers and innovators.” Ahead of the launch, faculty members and students from the Bengaluru and Manipal campuses completed specialised training at the MIT Bengaluru campus and the QuantrolOx laboratory at QuTech, TU Delft, in the Netherlands.

The programme developed practical capabilities in dilution refrigerator assembly, cryogenic systems, quantum control technologies, QPU measurements and superconducting quantum hardware, preparing the team to support the operations of the quantum facility at MIT Bengaluru.

topicPlan.title: 量子计算产业化是否已到晶体管时刻
topicPlan.angle: 量子计算正从实验室验证走向工程化和产业化，本篇回答这一转折是否真实发生及其瓶颈所在。值得现在写，因为印度MIT班加罗尔启用25量子比特教学研究设施、IonQ以最高13亿美元收购网络安全公司Elisity构建全栈平台，加上此前关于金刚石NV色心制造良率的讨论，共同显示产业化信号。但要区分教育设施、企业并购与真正的量产能力之间的差距，误差校正和制造良率仍是关键约束。

evidenceRecords.text: WARSAW, Poland — Norway’s Kongsberg has decided to build a new production facility for counter-drone systems in northern Poland, with plans to invest more than 200 million zloty ($51 million) in the plant.
The investment is connected to the company’s cooperation with Polish state-run defense group PGZ to deliver the San anti-drone system to the Polish military.
“We have been present in Poland for many years.

We think it’s important that we establish local sites in Poland,” Eirik Lie, the president and CEO of Kongsberg, told Defense News at the Warsaw Security Forum here on Oct. 12. “We are on good track for deliveries on the San program.
But also, we expect export contracts, so this enables us to be prepared for these exports from Poland.”

Under the San deal, valued at around PLN 15 billion ($3.8 billion), Kongsberg and PGZ are to supply 18 anti-drone batteries, 52 firing platoons, 18 command platoons, and 703 vehicles to the Polish military, according to data from Poland’s Ministry of National Defence.
The contract will be largely financed by loans that Poland has secured from the European Union’s Security Action For Europe (SAFE) scheme.
In a statement, the Norwegian group said it plans to sign a construction contract by the end of 2026 and begin work immediately afterward.
Serial production of counter-drone systems could begin in the first half of 2028.
The investment is expected to create more than 100 jobs in Poland once the plant reaches full capacity.

The Royal Navy Type 45 Destroyers appear to have received a new C-UAS system for self protection against drones.
Images released recently by the UK MoD show HMS Dauntless (D33) sporting two mystery containers that are likely acting as interceptor drone launchers.
The Ukrainian Navy ships were closing out Exercise Lion Protector, demonstrating their ability to safely manoeuvre as a small task group in company with a major warship, played by Dauntless.

The apparent lack of new, organic sensors indicate that the interceptors must be receiving targeting data from the Type 45’s existing suite, i.e. the Sampson multi-function radar, the S1850M long-range radar on the aft mast and/or the electro optic systems.
Adapting to new threats The presence of this new system on a Type 45 destroyer shows how navies are adapting to the new challenges posed by affordable drones.
This suggests HMS Dauntless could be the first Type 45 ship to trial the capability ahead of her High North deployment.

Drone attack and swarming tactics—extensively practiced by the Royal Navy and French Navy in dedicated exercises like Sharpshooter and WildFire and based on their experience from Red Sea deployments—highlighted a critical limitation in European navies’ VLS magazine depth (48 cells for Type 45 and Horizon destroyers, 32 cells for French Air Defence FREMMs).
To address this issue, the Royal Navy started transitioning toward DragonFire lasers and C-UAS helicopter (Martlet / LMM aboard Wildcat) .

The new C-UAS system spotted on Dauntless shows that the Royal Navy continues to transform the Type 45 from a conventional air-defence vessel into a highly resilient platform capable of surviving drone saturation.

history.title: US Army assesses Trust Automation’s integrated drone defence system
history.originalTitle: US Army assesses Trust Automation’s integrated drone defence system

evidenceRecords.text: Trust Automation has completed a US Army operational assessment of its Small-Unmanned Air Defense System (SUADS) during a National Training Center rotation at Fort Irwin, California.

Conducted with the 703rd Brigade Support Battalion, 2nd Armored Brigade Combat Team, 3rd Infantry Division, the assessment evaluated SUADS in a large-scale combat operations training environment under ongoing uncrewed aerial system (UAS) threats.

During the rotation, Trust Automation’s SUADS detected and engaged UAS between approximately two and six kilometres away, with potential coverage extending to approximately seven kilometres under favourable conditions, the company said in a 12 October press release.
Trust Automation’s integrated system combined radar, electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) sensors, NINJA and DroneBuster technologies.
SUADS brings multiple sensors and effectors into a single integrated system while enabling individual technologies to be added or upgraded as capabilities and threats evolve.
Trust Automation is also developing a mobile SUADS variant to support tactical units where forces move frequently.
For more information Trust Automation The September issue of the 2026 Unmanned Airspace Global Counter-UAS Systems Directory is now available.
The post US Army assesses Trust Automation’s integrated drone defence system first appeared on Unmanned airspace .
Interview participants were not aware of any enemy UAS that penetrated the defended area as a threat within the identified operational ranges without first being detected by the system.

MAJ Patrick Smith, Battalion Executive Officer said the system consistently provided layered surveillance, early warning, positive target identification and electronic defeat of hostile UAS before enemy systems could successfully conduct reconnaissance, target acquisition or attack missions.

history.title: Energy Department Announces New Genesis Mission Awards to Accelerate Scientific Capability
history.originalTitle: Energy Department Announces New Genesis Mission Awards to Accelerate Scientific Capability

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief The Department of Energy announced $159 million for 12 new Phase II Genesis Mission projects using AI and advanced computing to accelerate scientific research.
The projects include Harvard -led quantum computing error correction, Oak Ridge-led quantum magnet design, and efforts in fusion energy, biotechnology, geothermal energy and particle physics.

PRESS RELEASE — The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced 12 Phase II project awards for President Trump’s historic Genesis Mission, totaling $159 million, that will expand efforts to harness artificial intelligence (AI), advanced computing, and the nation’s world-class scientific capabilities to accelerate the pace of discovery.

By connecting America’s leading scientists with advanced AI, supercomputing, scientific data and DOE’s unique research infrastructure, the Genesis Mission is creating new capabilities to accelerate scientific discovery and expand the frontiers of U.S. science and technology.
The Department of Energy announced $159 million for 12 new Phase II Genesis Mission projects using AI and advanced computing to accelerate scientific research.
The projects include Harvard-led quantum computing error correction, Oak Ridge-led quantum magnet design, and efforts in fusion energy, biotechnology, geothermal energy and particle physics.
The awards build on the Genesis Mission’s growing portfolio of projects, first announced in July, to address critical national science and technology challenges.

history.title: Guest Post: Quantum Computing’s Transistor Moment
history.originalTitle: Guest Post: Quantum Computing’s Transistor Moment

evidenceRecords.text: In 2023, fabrication of NV centers was demonstrated at production scale under Germany’s national quantum computing initiative – the “transistor” manufactured repeatably rather than hand-assembled one defect at a time.

That figure deserves attention because almost no competing spin-defect platform has published a fabrication yield at all, and yield is the industrial question – how reliably usable qubits can be placed where they are wanted, at scale.
The first is a transistor moment.
In 2020, researchers in Leipzig, Germany, demonstrated the first working one-qubit diamond-based quantum computer – proof that the device physics worked outside a research setting.
Diamond – The Silicon of Quantum Computing?
Whether NV-center diamond is quantum computing’s silicon – the material system that wins the platform war – is an open question.
Silicon-vacancy and tin-vacancy centers in diamond have so far worked only at cryogenic temperatures, and other spin centers could eventually prove better.

history.title: IonQ Agrees to Buy Elisity in Cybersecurity Deal Worth Up to $1.3 Billion
history.originalTitle: IonQ Agrees to Buy Elisity in Cybersecurity Deal Worth Up to $1.3 Billion

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief IonQ has agreed to acquire cybersecurity company Elisity in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion, according to The Wall Street Journal.
IonQ CEO Niccolo de Masi said the acquisition aims to help customers address growing cybersecurity risks associated with AI and quantum computing.

IonQ has agreed to buy cybersecurity company Elisity in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion, expanding its security business as advances in quantum computing and artificial intelligence raise concerns about cyberattacks.
The transaction includes up to $150 million in additional payments tied to Elisity’s future performance, executives told The Wall Street Journal .
IonQ Chairman and CEO Niccolo de Masi told the newspaper that the acquisition reflects his expectation that companies will need stronger defenses as both technologies become more powerful.
“With Elisity and its team as part of IonQ , we will be well positioned to help customers protect critical infrastructure and enterprise networks throughout the transition to the quantum era.
IonQ is offering its customers a vertically integrated full-stack quantum platform across quantum computing, networking, sensing and cybersecurity.

Just as adding SkyWater Technology expanded IonQ’s capabilities in chip design, fabrication and packaging, Elisity will bring proven enterprise policy enforcement scale and deployment experience to our quantum security strategy and will give IonQ a strong growth platform to serve customers and create value for our shareholders,” Niccolo de Masi, Chairman and CEO of IonQ, said in a statement .
The Elisity agreement follows IonQ ’s $1.8 billion deal earlier this year to acquire chipmaker SkyWater Technology, likely its largest acquisition to date.

Insider Brief Manipal Academy of Higher Education launched Manipal House of Quantum, Quantum-Hub@MAHE, at MIT Bengaluru to support quantum engineering, hardware experimentation and indigenous technology development in India.
PRESS RELEASE — Manipal Institute of Technology, Bengaluru (MIT Bengaluru) on Tuesday launched Manipal House of Quantum, Quantum-Hub@MAHE.
Venkatesh, VSM (Retd.), 7th Vice Chancellor, MAHE and Advisor to MEMG; Prof. (Dr.) Madhu Veeraraghavan, Pro Vice Chancellor, MAHE Bengaluru; Dr. Karunakar A.

Kotegar, Pro Vice Chancellor, Technology & Science, MAHE; Dr. Raghavendra Prabhu, Additional Registrar, MAHE Bengaluru; Prof. Iven Jose, Director, MIT Bengaluru; and Mr. Vishal Chatrath, Co-Founder & CEO, QuantrolOX .

Located at the MAHE Bengaluru campus, the quantum facility at MIT Bengaluru provides students, researchers and industry collaborators with hands-on access to advanced quantum computing infrastructure, including quantum hardware, cryogenic systems and quantum control technologies.

Through an integrated academic framework, the facility will support experimentation, application development, deep-tech start-up incubation, component innovation, testing and translational research, positioning MIT Bengaluru as an emerging centre for quantum engineering and indigenous hardware development.
The facility commences operations with a 25-qubit open-architecture dilution refrigeration system designed for advanced training and experimentation.
Rao, Vice Chancellor, MAHE, said, “The MAHE House of Quantum at MIT Bengaluru reflects MAHE’s commitment to building advanced scientific capabilities and nurturing talent in emerging technologies.

By creating access to modern quantum infrastructure, we aim to contribute meaningfully to India’s growing quantum ecosystem.” Prof. (Dr.) Madhu Veeraraghavan, Pro Vice Chancellor, MAHE Bengaluru, said, “The Hub brings together education, research and innovation on a common platform.

It will create opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and help translate academic research into real-world technological impact.” Prof. Iven Jose, Director, MIT Bengaluru, said, “The quantum facility at MIT Bengaluru will provide students and researchers with valuable exposure to real quantum systems and engineering environments.

It marks an important step towards developing the next generation of quantum scientists, engineers and innovators.” Ahead of the launch, faculty members and students from the Bengaluru and Manipal campuses completed specialised training at the MIT Bengaluru campus and the QuantrolOx laboratory at QuTech, TU Delft, in the Netherlands.

The programme developed practical capabilities in dilution refrigerator assembly, cryogenic systems, quantum control technologies, QPU measurements and superconducting quantum hardware, preparing the team to support the operations of the quantum facility at MIT Bengaluru.
